editorial.headline: Corporate Hospitality Training: Open Nationally, Address-Sensitive in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This code covers company-run training that builds hospitality skills, with full foreign ownership open nationally and no Bali moratorium block at the stated risk level.
editorial.body:
This activity is about company-delivered job training designed to add practical skills and expertise in hospitality and hotel work. Its centre of gravity is not the operation of a hotel itself, but the structured development of people for that field: training organised by a company for workers or prospective workers who need stronger hospitality capabilities. That distinction gives the activity a clear professional purpose—building competence in an industry where service standards, operational discipline and specialist knowledge matter.

The record identifies the organiser plainly: the training is conducted by a company. It does not list any business-scale categories open to the activity, so the record offers no further scale-based distinction to draw. For a founder, that is a useful limit on the available evidence: the activity can be described confidently as corporate hospitality and hotel-work training, but not assigned to a particular scale category from this record alone.

At the national level, the activity is open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In practical terms, the record permits full foreign ownership nationally for this activity. The cited basis is Presidential Regulations 10/2021 and 49/2021. That national position is direct: this is not an activity presented here as subject to a reduced foreign-equity cap.

Bali adds an important location-specific reading without reversing that national openness. The Bali assessment is OK-or-higher-risk, and the stated reason is that medium-high and high-risk activities are not blocked by the moratorium. The province-wide rule blocks all low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities for PMA, but this activity is not identified as falling within that blocked band. The record nevertheless says to verify per address. That is not a new restriction invented around the code; it is the precise local caution supplied with the assessment. The honest conclusion is therefore straightforward: foreign ownership is fully open nationally, and this activity is not blocked by Bali’s stated PMA moratorium, subject to address-level verification.
